# `liber:gpio-device@1`

Generated reference for the `liber:gpio-device` package (`gpio-device.lsidl`). See [the LSIDL language](../../../LSIDL.md).

LiberSystem GPIO lines - the contract a `gpio-lines` controller serves on one LINE-SCOPED connection.  INPUT LINES ONLY, AND NEVER THE WHOLE CONTROLLER. The only connections to a `gpio-lines` provider are the ones DeviceManager mints with a SCOPED `CONNECT` naming one line - with its trigger, or for level reads alone - so every operation below is about that line. The controller holds each line for one connection at a time.  AN EVENT IS DELIVERED ONCE, AND THE LINE STAYS MASKED UNTIL IT IS ACKNOWLEDGED. So a level-triggered line that stays asserted cannot storm: it is delivered again after the acknowledgement, and not before. A connection scoped for level reads alone - an input `GpioIo`, a `GeneralPurposeIo` field's connection - answers the level and is delivered no event.

## Interfaces

### interface `gpio-device`

THE CONTRACT a `gpio-lines` publication serves on each line-scoped connection.

Request `[op u16][corr u32][args]`, reply `[corr u32][result]`.

| op | method | signature | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `line` | `line() -> result<gpio-line, error>` | What this connection is scoped to. |
| 2 | `level` | `level() -> result<bool, error>` | The line's level now. |
| 3 | `events` | `events() -> stream<gpio-event>` | The line's events. Refused - no stream - on a connection scoped for level reads alone. |
| 4 | `acknowledge` | `acknowledge() -> result<unit, error>` | The event delivered last is handled: the line may fire again. Refused when none is outstanding. |
